title: Hell House in Seymour gets new owners and a new life as paranormal destination

content:
A Connecticut home, made famous by paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren is getting a new chapter, and its new owners are hoping visitors will experience its haunted history for themselves.
Hell House, located at 89 Buckingham Road in Seymour, is now owned by paranormal investigator and content creator Elton Castee and comedian Matt Rife.
The two purchased the property after Castee says a terrifying overnight experience helped convince them to take on the historic home.
"The house legitimately tried to kill us," Castee said.

A terrifying night helped seal the deal
Castee said he and Rife were not initially looking to purchase another property after buying the Warren House in Monroe.
But someone representing Hell House reached out to see if they would be interested in purchasing the Seymour property as well.
Knowing the home's connection to the Warrens, Castee wanted to see it for himself before making a decision.
He arranged to spend the night there with a group of fellow YouTubers while filming for another creator's channel.
"We played it cool in email and we're like, 'Cool. Can we just spend the night in the house?'" Castee recalled.
During that overnight investigation, Castee said they experienced several inexplainable things but once a ball was pushed off the top of the stairs. He described that moment as a turning point, with members of the group deciding one by one to leave the property.
Castee also said a gas leak developed in the basement.
"Somehow a gas leak broke out in the basement, and had we actually slept here, we would've genuinely died," he said.
Castee believes leaving when they did may have saved their lives.
He also pointed out that the experience was unusual for him because it wasn't being filmed for his own channel, Overnight, which focuses on spending the night in reportedly haunted locations.
Had it been one of his own investigations, he said, they would have stayed.
Despite the experience, Castee said it didn't discourage him from purchasing the property.
Instead, he and Rife wanted to give the house the care it needed while preserving its history.

The history behind Hell House
Hell House became nationally recognized after being featured in the 2005 episode "Hell House" of the paranormal television series A Haunting.
The episode recounts the experiences of the Beckwith family, who moved into the 19th-century Connecticut home in 1998.
The family described increasingly disturbing activity inside the house, including claims that their children were attacked by unseen forces.
They eventually sought help from Ed and Lorraine Warren, the well-known paranormal investigators who became associated with some of the country's most infamous reported hauntings.
Their investigation included reported exorcisms.
Castee said he remembered seeing the episode years ago but didn't initially realize just how much history was tied to the property.
"It's crazy, 'cause it's the only place I can think of where I know an exorcism was performed and it's still standing today," he said.
For Castee, that history is something worth preserving.

Inside the renovations: Red rooms, spiritual sanctuaries and a séance room
Rather than simply restoring the house, Castee is incorporating details inspired by the stories told in the A Haunting episode.
Each room is being given a purpose, with plans to recreate some of the spaces and details associated with the Beckwith family's experiences.
One room, which Castee calls the Red Room, is being transformed with a red color scheme inspired by his interpretation of the room's history.
According to the accounts featured in the documentary, the room was where the family believed their son was locked away and where they used a knocking method to communicate with the reported paranormal presence.
Castee said he decided to take the room's name literally when planning the renovation.
Another room is being transformed into what he calls a spiritual sanctuary.
In the documentary, the family described using a green toy flashlight to comfort their youngest son when he became frightened, believing its light would keep the reported entity away.
Castee wants to incorporate that detail into the room's design.
In the kitchen, he plans to install a solid oak table inspired by accounts of the Warrens' investigation.
He also has plans for the basement, which will be transformed into a séance room.
The goal is to fill the property with paranormal investigation equipment and technology, giving overnight guests the opportunity to conduct their own investigations and document anything they experience.

When will Hell House open to overnight guests?
Castee said the goal is to give visitors the tools and opportunity to investigate the property themselves.
The experience will allow guests to explore the home's history while conducting their own paranormal investigations.
"We give everyone everything they could ever need to film, and that way if anything does happen, you can have it documented," Castee said.
For Castee, the project is about more than creating another paranormal attraction. He hopes to bring new life to a property with a well-known place in Connecticut's paranormal history.
"If we can bring life back into this and allow other people to experience it, that's like why we do this," he said.
Hell House begun welcoming overnight guests November 5, with prices starting at $666.
